newsitem.title: USA: Texas Stock Index ends win streak with March loss.
newsitem.headline: Texas Stock Index ends win streak with March loss.

text.p: The Texas Stock Index posted a loss in March, ending its three-month-string of record setting performances, State Comptroller John Sharp said Wednesday.
The TSI fell 4.7 points or 1.6 percent to 288.4, Sharp said. The index, however, is still 31.8 percent above the year-ago level.
"The TSI outperformed the Standard & Poor's 500 in March," the comptroller said. "The Standard & Poor's Index, which tracks a nationwide sampling of stock prices, fell 33.7 points, or 4.3 percent."

Texas-based energy stocks rebounded in March following the preceeding month's downturn. Those stocks rose five points, or 4.6 percent. The overall stock value of Texas energy companies is 18.5 percent higher than a year ago.

General business stocks' value on the TSI hit a record 219.1 for the second consecutive month. However, all six of the finance, insurance, and real estate stocks on the index lost value in March, with the sector declining 11.5 points, or 3.7 percent.
After a string of record setting months, the value of Texas-based technology stocks declined 27.3 points, or 3.7 percent. Seven of the sector's eight stocks posted losses.
The comptroller's office produces the monthly TSI to help gauge investor faith in Texas-based businesses.
The index is one of 10 components in the Comptrollers Index of Leading Texas Economic Indicators.
